description: Verify that DUT emits ICMP Destination Unreachable / Protocol Unreachable (type=3, code=2) when receiving an IPv4 packet whose upper-layer protocol is not supported — informs the sender to stop using that protocol (RFC 1122 §3.2.2.1 MUST)
approach:
[Objective]
When a packet arrives addressed to DUT but its IP-protocol number names a protocol DUT doesn't implement, RFC 1122 §3.2.2.1 requires DUT to respond with Destination Unreachable code 2 (Protocol Unreachable) so the sender knows to stop trying.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: IPv4 packet
   • dst_ip      = DUT IP
   • protocol    = some value DUT does not implement (e.g. 50 = ESP if no IPsec, 132 = SCTP if absent)

2. Observation (5 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: ICMP Destination Unreachable
      - type == 3
      - code == 2 (Protocol Unreachable)   ← key check
      - original IP header echoed in payload

[Pass condition]
DUT emits ICMP type=3 code=2 within the window.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_wrong_code — DUT emitted Destination Unreachable but with the wrong code (e.g. Port Unreachable code 3 instead)
• Fail_timeout — DUT did not emit Destination Unreachable within the window

verdicts.Pass: DUT emitted Destination Unreachable / Protocol Unreachable — normal
verdicts.Fail_wrong_code: Destination Unreachable emitted but with the wrong code
verdicts.Fail_timeout: DUT did not emit Destination Unreachable within the window
